items.stem: Which of the following statements about vectors is correct?
items.answer: The magnitude of A + B can never exceed |A| + |B|.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: "The magnitude of A + B can never exceed |A| + |B|." The other three are false.
options: The magnitude of A + B can never exceed |A| + |B|.
Vector addition is not commutative.
Multiplying a vector by a negative number does not change its direction.
Two vectors of unequal magnitudes can add to give zero.

items.stem: Why is the time interval a scalar even though it can be "positive" or "negative"?
items.answer: A scalar can have a sign; the sign is not a direction in space.
items.markingKey: Scalars have magnitude only (1 mark); sign ≠ spatial direction (1 mark).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Three vectors of magnitudes 4, 5 and 10 units can give zero resultant.
Reason (R): The resultant is zero only if the vectors can form a closed triangle.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: 4 + 5 < 10; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Two forces of 11 N and 11 N act on a body with an angle of 30° between them. Find the magnitude of the resultant and its angle with the 11 N force.
A force of 20 N acts at 30° to the positive x-axis in the x-y plane. Find its x- and y-components.
items.markingKey: Fx = F cos θ = 20 cos 30° = 17.3 N; Fy = F sin θ = 10.0 N.

items.stem: Three displacements are A = (−4î − 1ĵ) m, B = (5î − 1ĵ) m and C = (−3î + 5ĵ) m. Find the resultant displacement, its magnitude and the angle it makes with the x-axis.
items.markingKey: Add components: Rx = −2, Ry = 3 (1); |R| = √(4 + 9) = 3.61 m (1); θ = tan⁻¹(Ry/Rx) taking quadrant into account = 123.7° (1).

items.stem: Two vectors, each of magnitude 8 units, have a resultant of magnitude 8 units. Find the angle between them.
Tanvi walks 150 m north, then 150 m in a direction 45° east of north, and finally 300 m west. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant displacement.
items.markingKey: Take x east, y north: x = 150 sin 45° − 300 = −193.93 m; y = 150 + 150 cos 45° = 256.07 m (2); magnitude √(x² + y²) = 321 m (1); direction tan⁻¹(|x|/y) = 37.1° west of north (1).

items.stem: Can three vectors of magnitudes 2, 3 and 7 units add to give zero? Explain.
items.markingKey: For zero resultant they must form a triangle; 2 + 3 < 7, so no triangle (2 marks).

items.stem: Find the magnitude of the vector A = −2î + 3ĵ + 4k̂ and the unit vector along A.
Which of the following is a vector quantity?
items.markingKey: (b) Displacement has both magnitude and direction; the others are scalars.
options: work
displacement
distance
volume

items.stem: Two forces of 7 N and 9 N act at a point. Which of the following CANNOT be the magnitude of their resultant?
items.markingKey: (c) The resultant lies between |7 − 9| = 2 N and 7 + 9 = 16 N; 21 N is outside this range.
options: 3 N
9 N

items.stem: A force of 100 N acts at 37° to the positive x-axis in the x-y plane. Find its x- and y-components.
items.markingKey: Fx = F cos θ = 100 cos 37° = 79.9 N; Fy = F sin θ = 60.2 N.

items.stem: Find the magnitude of the vector A = 1î + 4ĵ + 2k̂ and the unit vector along A.

Assertion (A): A vector can have zero magnitude.
Reason (R): A null vector has zero magnitude and arbitrary direction.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Two forces of 6 N and 9 N act at a point. Which of the following CANNOT be the magnitude of their resultant?
items.markingKey: (a) The resultant lies between |6 − 9| = 3 N and 6 + 9 = 15 N; 20 N is outside this range.
options: 4 N
8 N

items.stem: Two forces of 7 N and 11 N act on a body with an angle of 135° between them. Find the magnitude of the resultant and its angle with the 7 N force.
Which of the following statements about motion in a plane is correct?
items.answer: The velocity of a particle is always along the tangent to its path.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: "The velocity of a particle is always along the tangent to its path." The other three are false.
options: The x and y motions of a projectile affect each other.
Relative velocity in two dimensions is found by adding the magnitudes of the two velocities.
The velocity of a particle is always along the acceleration.
The velocity of a particle is always along the tangent to its path.

items.stem: Explain why the time to cross a river is least when the boat heads perpendicular to the bank.
items.answer: Only the component across the river matters for crossing time; it is largest (the full boat speed) when heading perpendicular.
items.markingKey: Crossing time = width / perpendicular component (1 mark); maximum at 90° (1 mark).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A swimmer who heads perpendicular to the current crosses the river in the least time.
Reason (R): The current does not change the velocity component perpendicular to the bank.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Rain is falling vertically at 30 m s⁻¹. Varun rides a bicycle due east at 10 m s⁻¹. In which direction should Varun hold the umbrella?
items.answer: 18.4° from the vertical, tilted forward (towards the east)
items.markingKey: Relative velocity of rain = v_r − v_m; tan θ = v_m/v_r = 10/30 ⇒ θ = 18.4° from the vertical, towards the east (front).

items.stem: A boat can move at 5 m s⁻¹ in still water. It heads perpendicular to the bank of a river 1000 m wide flowing at 2 m s⁻¹. Find the time to cross and how far downstream it lands.
The position of a particle is r = 5t î + 3t² ĵ (in metres, t in seconds). Find its velocity and acceleration at t = 1 s, and the speed at that instant.
items.answer: v = 5î + 6ĵ m s⁻¹; a = 6ĵ m s⁻²; speed 7.81 m s⁻¹

items.stem: Why must a person walking fast in vertical rain hold the umbrella tilted forward?
items.answer: Relative to the person the rain comes at an angle from the front, so the umbrella must face that direction.
items.markingKey: v_rain,person = v_rain − v_person points forward-downward (1 mark); tilt forward (1 mark).

items.stem: A swimmer can swim at 2.5 m s⁻¹ in still water. A river 300 m wide flows at 1.5 m s⁻¹. In which direction must the swimmer head to reach the point directly opposite, and how long will it take?
items.markingKey: Along-stream component cancels: v_b sin θ = v_r ⇒ sin θ = 1.5/2.5 ⇒ θ = 36.9° (1.5); across speed √(v_b² − v_r²) = 2.00 m s⁻¹; t = 150 s (1.5).

items.stem: A particle starts from the origin at t = 0 with velocity 8î m s⁻¹ and moves in the x-y plane with a constant acceleration (3î + 2ĵ) m s⁻². Find its position and speed at t = 4 s.
A boat heads straight across a flowing river. Does it land directly opposite? Explain.
items.answer: No; the current carries it downstream while it crosses.
items.markingKey: Resultant velocity is the vector sum (1 mark); drift downstream (1 mark).

items.stem: The position of a particle is r = 9t î + 0.5t² ĵ (in metres, t in seconds). Find its velocity and acceleration at t = 1 s, and the speed at that instant.
items.answer: v = 9î + 1ĵ m s⁻¹; a = 1ĵ m s⁻²; speed 9.06 m s⁻¹

items.stem: Which of the following statements about motion in a plane is correct?
items.answer: Rain falling vertically appears slanted to a person walking in the rain.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: "Rain falling vertically appears slanted to a person walking in the rain." The other three are false.
options: Rain falling vertically appears slanted to a person walking in the rain.
The velocity of a particle is always along the acceleration.
Relative velocity in two dimensions is found by adding the magnitudes of the two velocities.
The x and y motions of a projectile affect each other.

items.stem: The velocity of B relative to A, v_BA, is related to v_AB by
items.markingKey: (c) Reversing the observer reverses the relative velocity.
options: v_BA = 2v_AB
v_BA = v_AB/2
v_BA = −v_AB
v_BA = v_AB

items.stem: For a projectile launched with speed u at angle θ, which quantity equals u² sin 2θ / g?
items.markingKey: (a) The horizontal range = u² sin 2θ / g.
options: horizontal range
time of flight
maximum height
maximum horizontal range

items.stem: Show that the ranges for launch angles θ and (90° − θ) are equal.
items.answer: sin 2(90° − θ) = sin(180° − 2θ) = sin 2θ, so R is the same.
items.markingKey: Use R = u² sin 2θ/g (1 mark); identity (1 mark).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A ball dropped and a ball thrown horizontally from the same height land at different times.
Reason (R): Both have the same vertical motion.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A ball is projected with a speed of 20 m s⁻¹ at 30° to the horizontal. Find its time of flight, maximum height and horizontal range. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.markingKey: T = 2u sin θ/g = 2.04 s; H = u² sin²θ/2g = 5.10 m; R = u² sin 2θ/g = 35.3 m.

items.stem:
At a district athletics meet, Farhan takes off for a long jump at 9 m s⁻¹ at 25° to the horizontal. Treat Farhan as a projectile (g = 9.8 m s⁻²).
(i) Find the horizontal component of take-off velocity. (ii) Find the time in the air. (iii) Find the length of the jump. (iv) What would the jump be at the same speed if the take-off angle were 45°?
items.markingKey: (i) u cos θ (1). (ii) 2u sin θ/g (1). (iii) u² sin 2θ/g = 6.33 m (1). (iv) u²/g = 8.27 m (1).

items.stem: A fielder throws a ball at 50 m s⁻¹. At what angles to the horizontal can it be thrown to land 220.9 m away on level ground? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
For a projectile, the horizontal range is 2 times the maximum height. Find the angle of projection.
A cricketer can throw a ball to a maximum horizontal distance of 90 m. How high above the ground can the cricketer throw the same ball (same speed)?
items.markingKey: R_max = u²/g = 90 m (1). Thrown vertically, H = u²/2g = R_max/2 = 45 m (2).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about projectile motion (air resistance neglected) is correct?
items.answer: Launch angles θ and (90° − θ) give the same range.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: "Launch angles θ and (90° − θ) give the same range." The other three are false.
options: The vertical component of velocity remains constant.
The velocity at the highest point is zero.
Launch angles θ and (90° − θ) give the same range.
The acceleration changes direction at the highest point.

items.stem: A fighter plane flies horizontally at an altitude of 1000 m with speed 200 m s⁻¹ and passes directly overhead an anti-aircraft gun. The muzzle speed of the shell is 450 m s⁻¹. At what angle with the vertical should the gun be fired to hit the plane? At what minimum altitude must the pilot fly to avoid being hit? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.answer: 26.4° with the vertical; above about 8.29 km
items.markingKey: Shell and plane must share the horizontal velocity: u cos θ = v ⇒ cos θ = 200/450 ⇒ θ = 63.6° with the horizontal, 26.4° with the vertical (2). Maximum height of shell = (u sin θ)²/2g = 8290 m ≈ 8.29 km (2); the pilot must fly higher (1).

items.stem: Show that the path of a projectile is a parabola. Derive the equation of its trajectory.
items.answer: y = x tan θ − gx²/(2u² cos²θ)
items.markingKey: x = u cos θ·t, y = u sin θ·t − ½gt² (2); eliminate t (2); form y = ax − bx² is a parabola (1).

items.stem: A stone is thrown horizontally with a speed of 10 m s⁻¹ from the edge of a cliff 4.9 m high. How far from the foot does it land? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.markingKey: t = √(2h/g) = 1.00 s (vertical motion); x = ut = 10 × 1.00 = 10.0 m.

items.stem: Why does a long jumper try to take off at nearly 45°?
items.answer: For a given take-off speed the horizontal range u² sin 2θ/g is greatest when sin 2θ = 1, i.e. θ = 45°.
items.markingKey: Range formula (1 mark); maximum at 45° (1 mark).

items.stem: Two balls are released together from the same height: one dropped, one thrown horizontally. Which lands first? Explain.
items.markingKey: Vertical motion is identical (initial vertical velocity 0, acceleration g) (2 marks).

items.stem: A stone is thrown horizontally with a speed of 12 m s⁻¹ from the roof of a building 20 m high. How far from the foot does it land? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.markingKey: t = √(2h/g) = 2.02 s (vertical motion); x = ut = 12 × 2.02 = 24.2 m.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The horizontal velocity of a projectile is constant.
Reason (R): There is no horizontal acceleration when air resistance is neglected.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Derive expressions for the time of flight, maximum height and horizontal range of a projectile launched with speed u at angle θ.
items.answer: T = 2u sin θ/g, H = u² sin²θ/2g, R = u² sin 2θ/g
items.markingKey: T from y = 0 (2); H from v_y = 0 (1.5); R = u cos θ × T (1.5).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about uniform circular motion is correct?
items.answer: The velocity at any point is along the tangent.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: "The velocity at any point is along the tangent." The other three are false.
options: The acceleration is along the tangent.
The velocity is constant.
The acceleration is zero because the speed is constant.
The velocity at any point is along the tangent.

items.stem: A body moves in a circle at constant speed. Why is it said to be accelerated?
items.answer: The direction of velocity changes continuously, so velocity changes and there is an acceleration (towards the centre).
items.markingKey: Velocity is a vector (1 mark); direction changes ⇒ acceleration (1 mark).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): In uniform circular motion the acceleration is constant.
Reason (R): The magnitude of centripetal acceleration v²/r is constant.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false because the direction of acceleration changes; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A car moves on a circular track of radius 200 m at a constant speed of 12 m s⁻¹. Find its centripetal acceleration.
A stone tied to the end of a string 120 cm long is whirled in a horizontal circle with constant speed. It makes 7 revolutions in 60 s. Find the magnitude and direction of its acceleration.
items.markingKey: ν = 7/60 = 0.1167 s⁻¹; ω = 2πν = 0.733 rad s⁻¹; a = ω²r = 0.645 m s⁻², directed towards the centre.

items.stem: An aircraft executes a horizontal loop of radius 0.5 km with a steady speed of 900 km h⁻¹. Compare its centripetal acceleration with the acceleration due to gravity.
A wheel completes one revolution in 5 s. What is its angular speed?
An aircraft executes a horizontal loop of radius 0.5 km with a steady speed of 720 km h⁻¹. Compare its centripetal acceleration with the acceleration due to gravity.
Show that the centripetal acceleration a = v²/r can also be written as ω²r.
items.answer: v = ωr, so v²/r = ω²r²/r = ω²r.
items.markingKey: v = ωr (1 mark); substitution (1 mark).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about uniform circular motion is NOT correct?
items.answer: The acceleration is zero because the speed is constant.
items.markingKey: (c) "The acceleration is zero because the speed is constant." is false; the other three are true.
options: The speed is constant but the velocity changes.
The magnitude of centripetal acceleration is v²/r = ω²r.
The acceleration is zero because the speed is constant.
The acceleration is directed towards the centre.

items.stem: An insect trapped in a circular groove of radius 20 cm moves along the groove steadily and completes 7 revolutions in 25 s. (i) What is its angular speed and linear speed? (ii) Is the acceleration vector constant? Explain.
items.answer: (i) ω = 1.76 rad s⁻¹, v = 35.2 cm s⁻¹ (ii) No; magnitude 61.9 cm s⁻² is constant but the direction changes
items.markingKey: (i) ν = 7/25; ω = 2πν = 1.76 rad s⁻¹ (1); v = ωr = 35.2 cm s⁻¹ (1). (ii) a = ω²r = 61.9 cm s⁻² towards the centre; its direction changes, so the vector is not constant (1).

items.stem: A car moves on a circular track of radius 25 m at a constant speed of 12 m s⁻¹. Find its centripetal acceleration.
Find the centripetal acceleration of a point at the equator due to the Earth's rotation about its axis. (R = 6400 km; take one day = 24 h)
items.markingKey: ω = 2π/86400 = 7.27 × 10⁻⁵ rad s⁻¹; radius of the circle = R cos λ = 6.40 × 10⁶ m; a = ω²R cos λ = 0.0338 m s⁻².

items.stem: Explain why two vectors of unequal magnitudes cannot give a zero resultant.
items.answer: Zero resultant needs equal magnitudes in opposite directions.
items.markingKey: Minimum |A + B| = | |A| − |B| | > 0 (2 marks).

items.stem: A ball is projected with a speed of 40 m s⁻¹ at 15° to the horizontal. Find its time of flight, maximum height and horizontal range. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.markingKey: T = 2u sin θ/g = 2.11 s; H = u² sin²θ/2g = 5.47 m; R = u² sin 2θ/g = 81.6 m.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A body in uniform circular motion is accelerated.
Reason (R): The direction of its velocity changes continuously.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: A particle starts from the origin at t = 0 with velocity 5î m s⁻¹ and moves in the x-y plane with a constant acceleration (1î + 3ĵ) m s⁻². Find its position and speed at t = 2 s.
items.markingKey: r = v₀t + ½at²: x = 5×2 + ½×1×4 = 12 m, y = ½×3×4 = 6 m (2); v = v₀ + at = 7î + 6ĵ; speed 9.22 m s⁻¹ (2).

items.stem: Rain is falling vertically at 25 m s⁻¹. Priya rides a bicycle due east at 8 m s⁻¹. In which direction should Priya hold the umbrella?
items.answer: 17.7° from the vertical, tilted forward (towards the east)
items.markingKey: Relative velocity of rain = v_r − v_m; tan θ = v_m/v_r = 8/25 ⇒ θ = 17.7° from the vertical, towards the east (front).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): In two-dimensional motion with constant acceleration, the path is always a straight line.
Reason (R): Motion in x and y can be treated independently.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false (a projectile's path is a parabola); R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: State the parallelogram law of vector addition.
items.answer: If two vectors are represented by two adjacent sides of a parallelogram from a common point, the diagonal from that point represents their resultant.
items.markingKey: Correct statement (2 marks).

items.stem: A ball is projected with a speed of 20 m s⁻¹ at 45° to the horizontal. Find its time of flight, maximum height and horizontal range. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)

items.stem: A wheel completes one revolution in 2 s. What is its angular speed?
Which of the following statements about vectors is NOT correct?
items.markingKey: (c) "Vector addition is not commutative." is false; the other three are true.
options: The magnitude of A + B can never exceed |A| + |B|.
Subtracting B is the same as adding −B.
Vector addition is not commutative.
A null vector has zero magnitude.

items.stem: A fighter plane flies horizontally at an altitude of 1500 m with speed 250 m s⁻¹ and passes directly overhead an anti-aircraft gun. The muzzle speed of the shell is 600 m s⁻¹. At what angle with the vertical should the gun be fired to hit the plane? At what minimum altitude must the pilot fly to avoid being hit? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.answer: 24.6° with the vertical; above about 15.2 km
items.markingKey: Shell and plane must share the horizontal velocity: u cos θ = v ⇒ cos θ = 250/600 ⇒ θ = 65.4° with the horizontal, 24.6° with the vertical (2). Maximum height of shell = (u sin θ)²/2g = 15200 m ≈ 15.2 km (2); the pilot must fly higher (1).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): At the highest point of its path, a projectile has zero velocity.
Reason (R): At the highest point the vertical component of velocity is zero.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false (the horizontal component remains); R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Two forces of 9 N and 6 N act on a body with an angle of 150° between them. Find the magnitude of the resultant and its angle with the 9 N force.
A car moves on a circular track of radius 50 m at a constant speed of 15 m s⁻¹. Find its centripetal acceleration.

Assertion (A): The magnitude of the resultant of two vectors lies between |A − B| and A + B.
Reason (R): The resultant is largest when the vectors are parallel and smallest when antiparallel.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A cricketer can throw a ball to a maximum horizontal distance of 70 m. How high above the ground can the cricketer throw the same ball (same speed)?
items.markingKey: R_max = u²/g = 70 m (1). Thrown vertically, H = u²/2g = R_max/2 = 35 m (2).

items.stem: For a projectile launched with speed u at angle θ, which quantity equals 2u sin θ / g?
items.markingKey: (d) The time of flight = 2u sin θ / g.
options: maximum height
maximum horizontal range
horizontal range
time of flight

items.stem: A stone tied to the end of a string 150 cm long is whirled in a horizontal circle with constant speed. It makes 20 revolutions in 50 s. Find the magnitude and direction of its acceleration.
items.markingKey: ν = 20/50 = 0.4 s⁻¹; ω = 2πν = 2.51 rad s⁻¹; a = ω²r = 9.47 m s⁻², directed towards the centre.

items.stem: Two forces of 15 N and 13 N act at a point. Which of the following CANNOT be the magnitude of their resultant?
items.markingKey: (a) The resultant lies between |15 − 13| = 2 N and 15 + 13 = 28 N; 1 N is outside this range.
options: 1 N
5 N

items.stem: Two vectors, each of magnitude 9 units, have a resultant of magnitude 10.8 units. Find the angle between them.
A person in a car moving east at 15 m s⁻¹ sees rain falling vertically. Relative to the ground, the rain
items.answer: has a horizontal component of 15 m s⁻¹ towards the east
items.markingKey: (a) v_rain = v_rain,car + v_car.
options: has a horizontal component of 15 m s⁻¹ towards the east
is at rest
falls vertically
has a horizontal component of 15 m s⁻¹ towards the west

items.stem: A ball is projected with a speed of 40 m s⁻¹ at 45° to the horizontal. Find its time of flight, maximum height and horizontal range. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.markingKey: T = 2u sin θ/g = 5.77 s; H = u² sin²θ/2g = 40.8 m; R = u² sin 2θ/g = 163 m.
